reason: I'll start gathering the study pages by combining the two natural history studies.
expectation: I expect a combined set of plant and pond study pages, though the exact result is unclear.

alternatives.reason: The weather and star records also seem related, but I'll group the biological studies first.

effect: The plant and pond pages are grouped, leaving the weather and star records to gather.
reaction: The grouping makes sense, though the result is unsurprising.
reason: This is the only offered combination and it groups the remaining records.
expectation: I expect a combined set of weather and star records.

effect: The weather and star records are grouped, so both sets of study pages are ready to gather.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should gather all the study pages.
expectation: I expect a collection containing all four subjects, possibly ready for binding.

effect: The pages are arranged by subject, and binding the encyclopedia is now the goal.
reaction: The organized collection is satisfying, though the result was expected.
reason: Thread should bind the collected pages, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the pages to be bound into an encyclopedia.

effect: The collected pages were stitched into an encyclopedia, completing the chapter.
reaction: The finished volume is a satisfying culmination of the earlier studies.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding the collected pages was most worthwhile because it brought the four subjects into one volume.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping the weather and star records was predictable and involved no meaningful choice at that point.

surprise.text: Nothing particularly surprised me; the combinations produced the groupings and binding I expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the menu supplied compatible combinations, so I did not have to discover how to group the pages.

continue.text: I would be unlikely to continue personally: assembling the encyclopedia was satisfying, but the mostly forced, predictable combinations offered little decision-making.
